short_term.note: The forecast of Météo-France's AROME-PI model for the next hours, worked out into levels by this API (the thresholds are in the descriptions of the fields). It is a model forecast, not an official warning: it is never part of local_alert_level, and the warnings of the national services are the nearby_hazards. Each value is the worst of a block of about 4 x 3 km around the point.

probabilities.attribution: Source: Météo-France, prévisions d'ensemble PE-AROME and PE-ARPEGE (https://portail-api.meteofrance.fr, Licence Ouverte 2.0), read by a vigie-meteo gateway; the PE-AROME probabilities are Météo-France's, the PE-ARPEGE ones are counted by Vigie among the 35 members; a model forecast, not an official warning
probabilities.note: Probabilities from Météo-France's ensemble forecasts: PE-AROME for the next 51 hours (windows of three hours) and PE-ARPEGE for the next 96 hours (windows of 24 hours), the probability of the block of 5 km or 10 km around the point: a chance for the area, which over-states the chance at one exact spot (measured against ground stations on one morning, ADR 0032). A window's probability is not the probability that it rains at some time of the day. A model forecast, not an official warning: it is never part of local_alert_level, and the warnings of the national services are the nearby_hazards. `rain_probability_pct` of `daily` stays Open-Meteo's (the highest hourly probability of the day, any amount) and is not merged with these: they answer a different question (an amount in a window), so the two numbers can differ.

correction.note: When applied, `heights`, `extremes` and `now` are the model's plus the gap that the nearest REFMAR tide gauge measured against the model, fading with time (ADR 0017). The gap is a mean over 12.4 hours (it cancels the model's own tidal error); heights before the last measure and the estimated coefficient are the model's. Ours, not SHOM's prediction.

tides.coefficient_note: Estimated by Vigie from the model's tide at Brest: 100 times the range of each semi-diurnal tide at Brest divided by 6.10 m. Not the official coefficient, which is SHOM's. In France the coefficient is used for the Atlantic, Channel and North Sea coasts, with the value of the high water at Brest; it says nothing of the Mediterranean or of other countries. SHOM's own definition (height of the high water above the mid-tide level, over a unit, times 100) was measured against this one on the tide observed at Brest and did not come closer (ADR 0018); the model's tide is not corrected, so the coefficient inherits the model's error.

coefficient_method.formula: 100 x (high water - mean of the two neighbouring low waters) / unit

tides.limits: The tide of the open coast near the point, from a model cell up to 30 km away. Inside a bay, a harbour, an estuary, a lagoon or a sound the real tide can come an hour or more later and be higher or lower, and the model can be wrong there; the weather (surge) is not included. Measured: on the coasts of France the high and low waters came within 3 to 23 minutes (median) of the observed ones; in harbours and bays of the United States up to 2 h 22 early (docs/measurements/tides-2026-10.md).
tides.disclaimer: Tide computed by Vigie from a global ocean tide model: not for navigation, and not an official tide table. Heights are relative to the mean sea level of the model, not to the chart datum of a port.
tides.attribution: Tides computed by Vigie from the EOT20 ocean tide model (Hart-Davis et al. 2021, DGFI-TUM, SEANOE, https://doi.org/10.17882/79489), CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); constants kept near the coasts and rounded by Vigie. Not for navigation

normals.note: Normals and records of the Météo-France station BIARRITZ-PAYS-BASQUE (64) (altitude 71 m), 2.5 km from the position, as its climate sheet gives them (edited 2026-11-06). A normal is the mean of the whole month, not of one day; a station at another altitude than the position can differ by several degrees.

forest_fire.note: Météo-France publishes the forest fire danger from June to September (about 17:00 local time); out of this season there is no map and no level is given. It is a danger of the department as a whole, in four levels, for the two days after the publication: not a warning, not a fire detected (see `fires_nearby` of `GET /v1/point`), and the local conditions of a forest can differ.

tide.note: Tide computed by Vigie from a global ocean tide model: not for navigation, and not an official tide table. Heights are relative to the mean sea level of the model, not to the chart datum of a port. Estimated by Vigie from the model's tide at Brest: 100 times the range of each semi-diurnal tide at Brest divided by 6.10 m. Not the official coefficient, which is SHOM's. In France the coefficient is used for the Atlantic, Channel and North Sea coasts, with the value of the high water at Brest; it says nothing of the Mediterranean or of other countries. SHOM's own definition (height of the high water above the mid-tide level, over a unit, times 100) was measured against this one on the tide observed at Brest and did not come closer (ADR 0018); the model's tide is not corrected, so the coefficient inherits the model's error.

rules.verdict: good, possible or poor, hour by hour: the verdict of an hour is the lowest of its criteria; a criterion whose value is unknown counts for nothing, except the one an activity cannot be judged without (kite: the wind; boat: the wind; shore fishing: the low water and the wind), which makes the verdict null; with none known the verdict is null
rules.headline: the best verdict among the daylight hours of the next 24 hours; best_slot: the longest run of consecutive daylight hours at that verdict, the first on a tie, and none when that verdict is poor
rules.surf: the rating of GET /v1/surf/spots/{id} (its rules are there), by its share of points: 75 % and over good, 50 % and over possible, less poor; with fewer than three criteria known, null. A primary swell worth 0 points (under 0.5 m, or 4 m and over) makes it poor whatever the other criteria give
rules.kite: wind within the range asked for (default 12 to 25 knots): good; within 3 knots of it: possible; else poor. Gusts above the mean wind by 5 knots or less: good; 6 to 8: possible; more: poor. Wind from the land side (offshore): possible at best
rules.boat: mean wind in Beaufort force (knots rounded): 4 or less good, 5 possible, 6 and over poor. Gusts: force 5 or less good, 6 to 7 possible, 8 and over poor. Sea (significant wave height): under 1.25 m good, under 2.5 m possible, else poor. With `boat_category` (EU Directive 2013/53/EU design categories): D (sheltered waters, up to force 4 and 0.5 m): wind 3 or less good, 4 possible; gusts 4 or less good, 5 possible; sea under 0.3 m good, under 0.5 m possible. C (inshore, up to force 6 and 2.0 m): wind 4 or less good, 5 to 6 possible; gusts 5 or less good, 6 to 7 possible; sea under 1.0 m good, under 2.0 m possible. B (offshore, up to force 8 and 4.0 m): wind 5 or less good, 6 to 8 possible; gusts 6 or less good, 7 to 9 possible; sea under 2.0 m good, under 4.0 m possible. A (ocean, over force 8 and 4.0 m): wind 6 or less good, 7 to 9 possible; gusts 7 or less good, 8 to 10 possible; sea under 3.0 m good, under 6.0 m possible
rules.shore_fishing: only in the 2 hours before a low water, judged at the middle of the hour; outside, poor. Coefficient estimated by Vigie (not SHOM's) of the Brest high water nearest in time to that low water: 70 to 99 good, 50 to 69 possible, 100 and over possible (the SNSM says 100 and over is a danger), under 50 poor. Wind force 5 or less good, 6 possible, 7 and over poor. Sea under 1.25 m good, under 2.5 m possible, else poor. Without the low water, null
rules.vigilance: an official coastal warning (phenomenon coastal; in France the wave-submersion vigilance) in force at the spot: red makes every verdict poor; orange keeps the boat and the shore fishing at possible at best; yellow changes nothing. Where the warnings could not be read, nothing is capped and vigilance.status says unknown

activities.limits: The verdicts are rules of Vigie, written in `rules`: a few thresholds on the swell, the wind, the tide and the official coastal warnings. They do not know the beach, the bottom, the shelter of a bay or the person who goes: a beginner and an expert do not have the same limits (the wind range of the kite is the one asked for). The swell is Météo-France's MFWAM model on a grid of about 8 km; the wind is a forecast at 10 m; the tide is computed from a global model and can be an hour late or more inside a bay. Hours are whole hours.
activities.disclaimer: Not for safety and not for navigation: look at the sea on the spot, the flags and the lifeguards, read the tide tables and the official warnings, and follow the instructions of the authorities.
